findingData.indexHeading: When and how much you send changes the cost
findingData.indexLine: Each finding is worked out from prices we store every hour. Each page shows the evidence, how it was worked out, and a file you can download.

findingData.notFound: We have no published finding at this address.
findingData.unit_price_changes: confirmed price changes by transfer apps since our record began
findingData.unit_weekend_increases: Saturday price rises that came back down by the Tuesday after
findingData.unit_sgd_per_month: Singapore dollars sent per month in total. Above it, stablecoins cost less for a transfer of five thousand to the Philippines.
findingData.title_price_changes: Transfer apps keep changing their prices
findingData.claim_price_changes: Transfer apps raise and cut what they charge to send money. The cheapest app when you compare may not be the cheapest when you send.
findingData.evidenceBasis_price_changes: Each row is one route: its confirmed changes, how many were rises or cuts, and how many apps moved.
findingData.method_price_changes: We record each app's cost every hour, for each amount sent, against the real exchange rate. A change counts only when one app's daily cost moved against every other app on the same route. It must move the same way, on the same day, by more than a small set amount. Moves that every app shares come from the exchange rate and never count. Each day needs several hourly readings, and a day is judged only once it has ended.
findingData.limits_price_changes: Each amount sent counts on its own. An app that changes its price at several amounts counts once for each. The number does not say how big any change was. It covers only the routes and apps we check, from the day each was added.
findingData.title_weekend_penalty: Some apps charge more on Saturday, then cut back
findingData.claim_weekend_penalty: A rise counts when an app charged more on a Saturday and came back down by Tuesday. If your transfer can wait, a weekday can cost less.
findingData.evidenceBasis_weekend_penalty: Each row is one route: its Saturday rises that came back, the cuts that undid them, and how many Saturdays we checked.
findingData.method_weekend_penalty: We start from the confirmed price changes. A rise counts when an app raised its price on a Saturday. The same app must then cut its price on the same route by the Tuesday after. Both moves must be in our data. We never assume a return from the rise alone.
findingData.limits_weekend_penalty: Each amount sent counts on its own. One Saturday rise counts once for each amount it showed up at. The number does not say how much more a Saturday cost. A route with few Saturdays checked has had little chance to show this.
findingData.title_volume_crossover: Stablecoins beat the cheapest app only above about {approx} a month, a figure worked out from the exchanges' published fee tiers
findingData.claim_volume_crossover: Sending five thousand Singapore dollars to the Philippines, a stablecoin would beat the cheapest app only above this monthly volume. Nobody in our data traded that much, and we never saw it happen: the figure is rebuilt from the exchanges' fee tiers. A stablecoin is a coin that stays worth one US dollar.
findingData.evidenceBasis_volume_crossover: Both rows are the same transfer, priced for two ways of buying on the exchange. Costs are in hundredths of a percent.
findingData.method_volume_crossover: We take every real check of sending five thousand Singapore dollars to the Philippines by stablecoin. For a given monthly volume, we look up the lower fee each exchange would charge. We rebuild each check's cost with those fees, from its own recorded prices. The number is the lowest volume where its usual cost drops below the cheapest app's usual cost. Both come from the same hours.
findingData.limits_volume_crossover: It covers one route and one amount. The number is rebuilt from real prices, never seen happening. Nobody in our data traded at that volume. It does not mean stablecoins are cheaper for most senders. Below that volume, the cheapest app costs less for this transfer.
findingData.limits_sgd_php_never_cheapest: It covers one route and only the hours we priced. It does not say a stablecoin can never win: on other routes it was the cheapest in some hours, and this route may change.
findingData.method_sgd_php_never_cheapest: Every hour we price a stablecoin path and each app for this route. A stablecoin counts as cheapest when its cost is below every app's cost in that hour. The count is the same one the home page and the routes page print.
findingData.evidenceBasis_sgd_php_never_cheapest: Each row is one amount sent from Singapore to the Philippines: the hours we priced, and the hours in which a stablecoin was cheapest.
findingData.unit_hours_stablecoin_cheapest: hours in which a stablecoin was the cheapest way to send
findingData.claim_sgd_php_never_cheapest: In no hour we priced did a stablecoin beat the cheapest app, at any of the five amounts. A stablecoin is a coin that stays worth one US dollar.
findingData.title_sgd_php_never_cheapest: Singapore to the Philippines: a stablecoin was never the cheapest way to send
